# py-ops - Python op layer (jix-py/src/ops/)

## Purpose

Turns arbitrary Python inputs (jix `Array`, numpy arrays/scalars, Python bool/int/float/complex,
lists) into `Operand`s, picks a typed Rust implementation at runtime from a per-op dispatch table
(casting operands as needed), broadcasts shapes NumPy-style, and wraps the jix_core lazy ops
(element-wise, comparison, bitwise, where, reductions, shape ops, sub_dtype, cast, asarray).
Nothing here reads array data; results are lazy `Array`s. All data-touching happens later in core.
Shared helpers live in jix-py/src/util.rs (normalize_dim*, ItemOrTuple, slice_unpack,
array_try_map) and are in scope for hunters of this subsystem.

## Contracts

Operand model (common/operand.rs:17-26). `Operand::PyArray(Py<Array>)` (a jix Array, keeps its
cached numpy dtype), `Operand::Array(ArrayAny)` (numpy array wrapped zero-copy in `Plain`), or
`Operand::Scalar{value, shape, precision, params}`. `precision == None` means "untyped Python
value"; typed numpy scalars / 0-d numpy arrays carry `Some(P1..P8)`.

Python -> Scalar (operand.rs:59-90): `bool` -> `Bool, Some(P1)` (typed on purpose); `int` fitting
i64 -> `Int, None`; int in (i64::MAX, u64::MAX] -> `UInt, None`; any other int -> `Float, Some(P8)`
(OverflowError if beyond f64); `float` -> `Float, None`; `complex` -> `Complex, None`. np.generic
(incl. np.float64, a float subclass) skips this and goes through `np.asarray` -> 0-d path
(operand.rs:101-163), giving a typed Scalar. Non-scalar inputs become `Plain` storage
(operand.rs:165-197): ndim checked (`check_ndim`, util.rs:41), negative strides rejected
(operand.rs:172-179), zero strides accepted.

Rank/precision (common/dtype_promote.rs). `scalar_kind_to_rank_precision` (operand.rs:342-352);
complex precision = itemsize/2. `CastKind::is_cast_allowed` (dtype_promote.rs:62-142):
- Untyped Python Int is remapped to UInt when the target is unsigned (67-73): an untyped int fits
  both signed and unsigned slots; value fit is checked later, not here.
- `None`: same rank and (untyped or equal precision) (76-78).
- `Safe` (79-135): never down-rank; Bool -> anything; same rank needs `p <= dst`; UInt -> Int
  needs `p.higher() <= dst` (u64 -> any int: false); Int/UInt -> Float/Complex: `dst == P8` always
  allowed (lossy u64/i64 -> f64 is accepted), else `p.higher() <= dst`; untyped always allowed.
- `Unsafe` (136-140): anything except Complex -> UInt/Int/Float.

Dispatch (common/dispatch.rs:180-233). `dispatch_args` requires every operand to have a plain
scalar dtype (struct / inner-shape dtypes -> `unsupported_dtype_error`, a RuntimeError). If ALL
operands are untyped, they are defaulted to P8 (Bool stays P1) for selection only (317-329). If
no operand is f16 (Float/Complex with P2), any descriptor mentioning F16 is skipped (199-208,
332-336). First descriptor whose every input passes its CastKind wins; operands are cast with
`Operand::cast` and the closure runs. A cast failure (e.g. OverflowError) is returned, NOT a
fall-through to the next descriptor. Order of a table is therefore semantics.

`Operand::cast` (operand.rs:200-232): untyped Scalar ints are bounds-checked against an integer
target (`check_int_in_bounds`, 375-405, OverflowError "out of bounds"); floats/complex/bool never
are. Scalars are converted value-wise (`Scalar::cast`, 407-460) and rebuilt at the target dtype
(no `Cast<Scalar>` view - tests assert this). Arrays go through `cast_impl` (ops/mod.rs:104-180).
The `into_typed::<T>().unwrap()` calls in dispatch.rs:74,101-102,141,171-172 rely on this cast
producing exactly `T::DTYPE`; complex -> non-bool is never requested because Safe/None/Unsafe
tables never allow it (cast_impl returns TypeError for it, mod.rs:138-157,175-179).

Promotion for where/stack/concatenate (dispatch.rs:236-314). If every operand is an array and all
dtypes are equal (struct dtypes included) -> no cast. Otherwise the first kind in
[Bool,U8,I8,U16,I16,U32,I32,U64,I64,(F16 only if an f16 input),F32,F64,C64,C128] that every
operand Safe-casts to; none -> RuntimeError "does not support operands with dtypes".

Broadcasting (common/broadcast.rs). `broadcast_shapes` (100-132) is right-aligned NumPy rules,
0 broadcasts with 1, result ndim = max input ndim (so <= NDIM_MAX). `broadcast_operand` (38-93)
returns the operand untouched if its shape already matches, else prepends dims with
`insert_dim(0..k)` then `Broadcast::new_array`; a Scalar only gets its `shape` field replaced.
Order in callers: define_op2/power/multiply/clamp/isclose broadcast BEFORE dispatch; `where`
broadcasts all three then promotes x/y (where_op.rs:66-67). Unary ops/reductions never broadcast.

What core validates (so the Python layer may skip it): ReductionOp dims OOB/duplicate/empty-dim
(jix/src/ops/reduction.rs:121-150); InsertDim positions are OUTPUT positions, any order,
duplicates rejected, check_ndim (insert_dim.rs:59-80); PermuteDims length/range/dup
(permute_dims.rs:51-72); RemoveDim range/dup/len==1 (remove_dim.rs:56-75); Reshape element count
via checked product (reshape.rs:57-63); Stack/Concatenate shapes+dtypes equal and check_ndim
(stack.rs:62-95, concatenate.rs:70-110); Broadcast same ndim and 1->n rule (broadcast.rs:54-80);
Repeat/Tile checked_mul; Roll handles len 0 (roll.rs:51-55); Where cond bool and x/y same dtype.
What core does NOT validate and Python must: DimArray capacity (ArrayVec collect panics past
NDIM_MAX), Python int ranges, numpy buffer validity (byte order, bool bytes), slice bounds.

Errors: core `jix_core::Error` -> `RuntimeError`, except `Arithmetic` -> `FloatingPointError`
(util.rs:54-64). Python-side validation raises ValueError / IndexError / TypeError /
OverflowError directly.

## Unsafe inventory

- operand.rs:181-183 `&*array.as_array_ptr()` then read `fields.data`. Assumes the PyArrayObject
  is live: `array` is a `Bound` held under the GIL in the same scope. Sound.
- operand.rs:185-194 `Plain::new(array.unbind(), data_ptr, shape, strides, dtype, params)`.
  Contract (jix/src/storage/plain.rs:108-115; plain_ndarray_ptr adds "elements valid for dtype",
  :415-421; alignment NOT required, :97-100): (a) pointer outlives storage - the `Py<PyUntypedArray>`
  is stored as `allocation`, keeping the numpy array and its base alive; (b) every index in shape
  is readable at the given byte strides - inherited from numpy's own shape/strides invariant
  (as_strided can violate it, as in numpy); (c) strides non-negative - checked at 172-179;
  (d) ndim <= NDIM_MAX - checked at 166. NOT established: element validity for `bool` (numpy bool
  buffers can hold bytes other than 0/1 via `.view(bool)` / `frombuffer`), native byte order
  (dtype_from_numpy, jix-py/src/dtype.rs:101-215, never looks at byteorder), and absence of
  concurrent writes from Python while jix reads with the GIL released.
- util.rs:359-405 `array_try_from_fn` and 408-445 `array_try_map` (used by broadcast_operands
  and operands_dtype_promotion on `[Operand; N]`, which needs_drop). Assumes each src index is
  `ptr::read` once and `DropGuard.next` is advanced before calling `f`, so on Err/panic exactly
  `src[next..]` is dropped and the `InitGuard` drops initialized outputs. Reviewed sound; recheck
  if edited.
- util.rs:25 `PySlice_Unpack` FFI: live slice, valid out-pointers, error fetched on < 0.
- util.rs:88-152 numpy_empty / numpy_empty_ordered / numpy_reshape FFI: used by array.rs, not by
  ops; listed for completeness.

## Edge-case surface

- Python ints: value vs. dispatch pick (u8 array + 256 / -1 -> OverflowError, by design); ints in
  (i64::MAX, u64::MAX] are `UInt` and fit only u64/float slots; ints beyond u64 become typed f64;
  python bool is typed (P1) so `True + 1` is NOT the all-untyped 64-bit case.
- f16 skip: only Float/Complex with precision P2 count as "f16 input"; an untyped float next to an
  f16 array stays f16 (can overflow to inf, by design).
- Scalar -> f16 conversion goes through core `Cast<f16>` = `f16::from_f32(x as f32)`
  (jix/src/ops/cast.rs:59, :543): double rounding for f64 inputs.
- 0-d inputs: numpy 0-d -> Scalar (typed); jix 0-d Array stays PyArray. Single-dim reductions
  and repeat/roll/tile with `dim=None` require ndim == 1 (util.rs:170-182).
- Reductions: `dim=()` -> no-op reduction; `dim=None` -> all dims (0-d -> []); duplicates and OOB
  -> core error (RuntimeError, not ValueError); keepdim re-inserts at the normalized input
  positions via InsertDim, which accepts unsorted positions (reduction.rs:7-23, 70-72, 116-118).
- Dim normalization: `normalize_dim` takes i32 (larger Python ints -> OverflowError from pyo3);
  `normalize_dims` does not check `dims.len()` against NDIM_MAX (util.rs:185-192) - callers must
  pre-bound it (`ItemOrTuple::into_dim_array` does, util.rs:256-274; `Vec<i32>` in permute_dims
  does not).
- Indexing (parse_basic_index, shape_ops.rs:205-350, also used by Array.__getitem__/numpy() via
  array.rs:180-214): strict bounds; step must be 1; `extract::<i64>` accepts Python bool and any
  `__index__` object; omitted/`sys.maxsize`/huge stop is unpacked to PY_SSIZE_T_MAX and replaced by
  `len` (util.rs:30-32), so huge explicit stops are silently clamped while `stop = len + 1` raises.
  Dims longer than i64::MAX (reachable: u8 array repeat/tile to > 2**63) are cast `as i64`
  (281, 289, 305, 342) and flatten casts `size as i64` (795).
- reshape (703-763): u64 `known_size *= dim` can overflow (panics in debug builds - maturin
  develop is debug - wraps in release, then core's checked product rejects); `-1` with a zero-size
  array is rejected (740).
- stack/concatenate: python scalars allowed (become 0-d, then ndim check); single array fast paths
  (872-876, 954-958); promotion happens before the ndim check; result numpy dtype is taken from
  the first (post-promotion) array.
- `out=` is not handled in ops/ at all; it lives in array.rs (`check_output_array`, 216-286).

## Intentional behaviors (do not report)

- Dispatch picks the first table entry, and a value that does not fit raises OverflowError
  instead of trying the next entry: `power(int_arr, -1)` raises, `u8_arr + 256` raises,
  `bool_arr + 1000` raises (test_type_promotion.py:405-500, 723-727).
- Untyped Python int matches unsigned slots (u64 + 1 stays u64; `2 ** u8_arr` is u8)
  (test_type_promotion.py:457-481, 692-707).
- Python bool is typed: `True + 1 -> u8`, `True + 1.5 -> f32` (test_type_promotion.py:388-396).
- No operand is f16 -> never f16: `i8 + 1.5 -> f32`, `i8 / i8 -> f32`, `sqrt(u8) -> f32` (numpy:
  f64 / f16) (test_type_promotion.py:17-24, 346-352, 599-622). All-untyped operands default to
  64-bit (`add(1, 1.5) -> f64`).
- u64 with any signed int -> f64, lossy above 2**53 (test_type_promotion.py:203-205).
- `negative(u8) -> i16`, `negative(u64) -> f64`, `negative(bool) -> i8` (op1.rs:25-29, tests 119-145).
- `bool_arr + bool_arr -> u8` (no bool impl in add) (test_type_promotion.py:230).
- `power(x, 0.5)` for a scalar 0.5 uses sqrt: `-inf -> nan`, `-0.0 -> -0.0`, unlike general pow
  (test_op2.py:643-651); `x ** 2` scalar uses square; tables mirror power's pairs so dtypes match
  (op2.rs:632-689, test_op2.py:529-640). Integer base with negative typed exponent gives 0 +
  `invalid` (op2.rs:550-552). Complex power unsupported.
- `multiply(a, a)` with the same object goes to `square` (op2.rs:170-178).
- Comparisons / maximum / clamp / isclose bounds-check Python ints too (test_type_promotion.py:405-436).
- `where` requires a bool condition (where_op.rs:16-17); x/y promote like dispatch.
- `sum(bool) -> u64`, `product(bool)` unsupported, argmax/argmin return u64
  (reduction.rs:282-286, 320-324, 217; test_reduction.py:522-527).
- Slicing: strict bounds, no clamping, step must be 1 (shape_ops.rs:120-121; test_slice.py:212-246).
- broadcast() needs the same ndim; concatenate needs the same ndim; repeat/roll/tile with
  `dim=None` only for 1-D; tile takes a single int (shape_ops.rs:32-34, 806-807, 985, 1119-1120, 1172-1174).
- dims arguments accept an int or a TUPLE only (lists/ndarrays rejected) (util.rs:230-252,
  test_bad_input.py:65-91). Exception: permute_dims takes `Vec<i32>` (any sequence).
- asarray ignores `params` for an existing jix Array (as_array.rs:30-31).
- All core errors surface as RuntimeError (test_type_promotion.py:921-928).

### Changed since generation (dbb99e2 #85, 5b3a9f5 #86) - these supersede conflicting bullets above
- Unsigned ints negate as the signed int of the SAME width (wrapping): `negative(u8) -> i8`,
  `negative(u64) -> i64` (was i16 / f64). `bool - bool -> i8`.
- `floor` / `ceil` / `round` return integer arrays as is; `real` returns non-complex arrays as is.
- A Python int outside int64 raises OverflowError ("out of bounds") with every array dtype,
  including float and uint64 arrays and all-scalar calls (it used to become an f64 scalar).
- A dtype mismatch raises TypeError (was RuntimeError), e.g. where / concatenate / stack of a
  struct and a scalar dtype ("does not support operands with dtypes").
- `broadcast()` inserts leading dims when ndim differ (shared `broadcast_array_impl` in
  jix-py/src/ops/, also used by operand broadcasting in ops/common/broadcast.rs).
- New Python functions `jix.log2` / `jix.log10` (aliases of `jix.log(x, base=...)`,
  jix-py/python/jix/__init__.py).
- reshape's -1 inference checks the known-size product for overflow (ValueError).
- `params={"block_shape": [...9 entries]}` raises instead of PanicException (try_block_shape).
Line numbers in this doc refer to bb1ee2c; jix-py/src/ops/op1.rs and shape_ops.rs moved the most.

### Changed in c009869 (#87) - supersedes conflicting statements above (line numbers above refer to bb1ee2c)
- Slices with start == dim length are allowed (zero-length dims too). reshape(-1) of a zero-size
  array infers 0. permute_dims with more than 8 entries raises. NDIM_MAX items plus an Ellipsis are
  accepted. A huge slice stop clamped by PySlice_Unpack is treated as stop = len.
- uint64 vs int64 comparisons use exact kernels. jix-py/src/ops/common/mod.rs shrank (~60 lines).

### Changed in 6f8e220 (#88) and 7e93487 (#89) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- #89: bitwise / cmp / where / reduction wrappers dispatch on `bool8` (jix-py ops changed). Check that
  numpy bool inputs holding bytes other than 0/1 give numpy's results.

### Changed in 691e11b (#91) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- Two-bound `clamp` lists bool8 first, so `clamp(bool, min, max)` stays bool (K75).
- `slice` uses the fallible `SliceSpec::new(..)?`. `OpDescriptor`'s input-dtype collection no longer
  unwraps (dispatch.rs:186-192).
- Open and tracked in todo.md: `bitwise_rotate_left/right` promotion of Python ints (K76).

### Changed in df2f918 (#92) - supersedes conflicting statements above
- `jix.log(x, base)` raises ValueError for base <= 0 or == 1 (K107); base e / 2 / 10 dispatch to
  Ln / Log2 / Log10, any other base is computed in f64 and cast once (K92).
- `cast_impl` uses the fallible `Cast::new_array` (K88). `jix.cast` is `asarray(array, dtype)`.
- `asarray(value, dtype=)` for a value that is not a jix or numpy array goes through
  `numpy.asarray(value, dtype=)` first, so numpy's range checks apply to Python ints (K96).
- Operand's numpy -> Plain conversion moved to `plain_from_numpy` (operand.rs:419-490).

## Hot spots

1. Dispatch tables (op1/op2/cmp/bitwise/reduction): is the order right for every input pair, and
   does each (a, b) pair list match the core op's trait bounds? Hand-written tables (log
   op1.rs:303-339, clamp cmp.rs:415-442, isclose cmp.rs:548-602, power op2.rs:597-677,
   rotate bitwise.rs:428-491) are the risky ones; macro tables are type-consistent by
   construction (desc dtype and `into_typed` come from the same `T`).
2. `is_cast_allowed` + `cast_python_scalars_to_default_precision` + f16 skip interact: find an
   input combo where the chosen dtype silently loses value (no OverflowError) - e.g. Scalar::UInt
   untyped vs float slots, typed scalars under `Unsafe`, P2 precision on a complex.
3. `Operand::cast` / `Scalar::cast` / `into_array` (operand.rs:200-302, 407-460): does the
   rebuilt Scalar always have the exact dtype the descriptor expects (else `unwrap` panics in
   dispatch.rs)? f16 double rounding; complex64 rounding; `absolute` on a Scalar keeps the old
   precision while switching Complex -> Float (op1.rs:633-647).
4. numpy -> Plain boundary (operand.rs:165-197): byte order, bool validity, unaligned and
   overlapping/zero strides, struct dtypes whose numpy itemsize/offsets differ from jix's
   (dtype.rs only `debug_assert`s equality, dtype.rs:206-213).
5. Shape-op argument normalization (shape_ops.rs): ArrayVec capacity, `as i64`/`as u64` casts,
   empty dims (len 0) in slicing, reshape inference, stack single-array path vs `dim == ndim`.
6. Promotion in where/stack/concatenate (newest code, bb1ee2c): numpy dtype attached to the
   result (first array only), PyArray vs Array identity after broadcasting, mixed scalar/array lists.

### Suspicions (unverified)

- jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:606 - `permute_dims` takes `Vec<i32>`; `normalize_dims`
  (util.rs:185-192) collects into `DimArray` (ArrayVec cap 8) without a length check, so
  `permute_dims(a2d, [0]*9)` (all in range) should panic (PanicException) instead of raising.
- jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:314 - `start_norm >= len` rejects valid empty slices: `a[:]` /
  `a[0:0]` on a length-0 dim and `a[len:len]` raise IndexError (also via `__getitem__`).
- jix-py/src/dtype.rs:136-176 via operand.rs:165-197 - byte order is ignored: a big-endian numpy
  array (`'>i4'`, common from FITS/HDF5) is read as little-endian, silently wrong values.
- jix-py/src/ops/mod.rs:96-100 and as_array.rs:63-69 - the user's numpy dtype is attached
  verbatim; `jix.cast(a, '>i4')` / `asarray(x, dtype='>f8')` makes `.numpy()` allocate a
  big-endian array (array.rs:551) that jix fills with little-endian bytes.
- jix-py/src/ops/common/operand.rs:185 - numpy bool buffers are wrapped without checking bytes
  are 0/1; core reads them as Rust `bool` (invalid value = UB) e.g. `np.uint8([2]).view(bool)`.
- jix-py/src/ops/cmp.rs:439 - clamp table lists `bool` last, so `clamp(bool, lo, hi)` returns u8
  while `clamp(bool, lo)` / maximum / minimum return bool (#82 moved bool first only there).
- jix/src/ops/cast.rs:59 (hit from operand.rs:427) - f64 -> f16 via f32 double-rounds;
  `f16_arr + x` for a Python float near an f16 tie can differ by 1 ulp from numpy.
- jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:245 - Python `True`/`False` index is taken as int 1/0 (numpy
  treats a bool scalar index as a new-axis mask); np.bool_ raises TypeError instead.
- jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:724 - `known_size *= dim as u64` unchecked; panics in debug builds
  for e.g. `reshape(a, (2**40, 2**40, -1))`.
- jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:740 - `reshape(zero_size, (-1, 3))` raises; numpy returns (0, 3).
- jix/src/ops/shape_ops/concatenate.rs:110 - `shape[dim] += shape_i[dim]` unchecked before
  `check_shape_overflow`; reachable from jix.concatenate with dims > 2**63 (u8/bool arrays).
